title: 3D- (H-theta-phi) magnetic phase diagram of antiferromagnetic metal GdB6 with electron and lattice instability
authors: A. N. Azarevich, A. V. Bogach, T. F. Garipova, V. V. Voronov, M. Rajnak, S. Gabani, K. Flachbart, N. B. Bolotina, O. N. Khrykina, V. M. Gridchina, A. Yu. Tsvetkov, S. Yu. Gavrilkin, N. E. Sluchanko
abstract: The origin of charge transport and magnetization anisotropy was studied in GdB6, an antiferromagnetic (AF) metal (Néel temperature TN ~ 15.5 K) with cubic lattice and Gd S-type magnetic ions. Both small static Jahn-Teller distortions and nanoscale electronic instabilities (dynamic charge stripes) were found in precise low temperature X-ray diffraction measurements. The detailed magnetic field (H) vs temperature (T) phase diagrams were constructed with two main magnetic phases AF(I) and AF(II). Using the angular phi-dependences of magnetoresistance and magnetization, impeller-type patterns of the H-phi magnetic phase diagrams in the (110) and (111) planes were found at helium temperatures, which included the AF phases I and II separated from each other by radial and circular boundaries. The results argue in favor of the important role of the spin density wave 5d- component in the magnetic structure of AF(II) state. Charge fluctuations in stripes are proposed to be responsible for the suppression of the Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yoshida (RKKY) indirect exchange between the first and second neighboring Gd3+ ions located along the <100> and <110> directions. These dynamic charge stripes and vibrationally coupled Gd-Gd pairs produce unusual anisotropy of charge scattering and the impeller-type diagrams in GdB6 with S-type magnetic ion.
summary: This experimental work characterizes the complex magnetic phase diagram of the antiferromagnetic metal GdB6 by measuring magnetization and resistivity under varying magnetic fields and angles. The authors find evidence of dynamic charge stripes and structural distortions that fundamentally alter the magnetic exchange interactions. This work provides a detailed picture of how coupled electron and lattice instabilities govern the material's unusual magnetic anisotropy.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin of charge transport and magnetization anisotropy in the antiferromagnetic (AF) metal GdB6, focusing on the role of electron and lattice instabilities.
main_result: The research identified 'impeller-type patterns' in the H-phi magnetic phase diagrams and proposed that dynamic charge stripes suppress the RKKY exchange, leading to unusual charge scattering anisotropy.
method: The study employed detailed measurements of resistivity, magnetization, and X-ray diffraction at low temperatures to map out complex magnetic and electronic phase diagrams.
model_or_system: The physical system is GdB6, an antiferromagnetic metal with a cubic lattice and Gd S-type magnetic ions. The analysis focuses on the interplay between magnetic ordering (AF(I) and AF(II) phases) and electronic instabilities like dynamic charge stripes.
key_observables: Magnetization (M), resistivity ($ho$), magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$), and structural distortions detected via X-ray diffraction.
important_parameters: Low temperatures (down to helium temperatures), external magnetic fields up to 180 kOe, and angular dependence ($\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the importance of the spin density wave 5d- component in the AF(II) state and links charge fluctuations in stripes to the observed magnetic anisotropy.
figures_summary: Figures detail H-T, H-phi, and 3D H-theta-phi phase diagrams, showing transitions between AF phases I and II, and mapping angular dependencies of resistivity and susceptibility.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements across various magnetic field, temperature, and angle regimes to construct comprehensive magnetic phase diagrams, linking structural distortions (Jahn-Teller) to electronic instabilities (charge stripes) and magnetic behavior.
why_interesting: The detailed mapping of magnetic phase diagrams and the explicit connection drawn between charge density wave physics (stripes) and magnetic anisotropy are highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in strongly correlated materials.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Temperature dependences of (a) the specific heat C(T, H0) in various magnetic fields H0 ≤ 90 kOe, and zero field resistivity (T), and (b) the Seebeck coefficient S(T) and magnetic susceptibility 4πM/H(T, H0 = 100 Oe) for H||[001], [112], [111] and [110] in GdB6. I, II and P denote two AF and paramagnetic phases, TN and T* are the temperatures of magnetic phase transitions.

Fig. 3. Temperature dependences of susceptibility 4πM/H0(T, H0) of GdB6 (a) in the range T ≤ 18 K in magnetic field up to 180 kOe for the principal direction H||[001], and (b) in magnetic field up to 50 kOe for H||[111]. Panels (c) - (d) show field dependences of the susceptibility at temperatures fixed in the range 2-16 K for (c) H||[001] in the interval H ≤ 5 kOe, where the hysteresis is observed, and for (d) H||[111] up to 50 kOe. Vertical arrows mark the magnetic phase transitions I-II and I-P.

Fig. 4. Magnetic field dependences of resistivity (H, T0) of GdB6 at fixed temperatures T0 ≤ 16 K for principal field directions H||[001] (a), H||[110] (b) and H||[111] (c). Arrows mark the magnetic phase transitions in the AF state, Roman numerals denote the magnetic phases (see Fig. 5). HN and H* denote the critical fields of the AF phase transitions at TN (I-P) and T* (I-II).

Fig. 5. Magnetic H-T phase diagrams of GdB6 along three principal directions of the external magnetic field (a) H||[001], (b) H||[110] and (c) H||[111]. Roman numerals denote different magnetically ordered phases, P- paramagnetic state. Vertical dashed line marks T0 = 5 K, which corresponds to the results of angular measurements (Figs. 6-7) and to the H-φ diagram in the (110) and (111) planes (Figs. 8-9). Low field hysteresis areas (phases Ih and IIh) are shaded.

Fig. 6. (Color online). Temperature dependences of magnetic susceptibility in the range T≤ 18 K for magnetic field intensity H0 = 1 kOe (a), 5 kOe (b) and 18 kOe (c) with rotation of H in the (1-10) plane. Radial dotted lines show the principal directions when vector H is aligned with the principal axes in the cubic lattice. Circular dotted lines mark TN, T* and Т0 = 5 К. Roman numerals I and II denote different magnetically ordered phases. The amplitude of 4πM/H(φ, H0, T0) is shown by color.
